messages:
taylor: Heads-up — we had a noisy GPU yesterday in us-west-2: multiple Xid 13/31 spikes and a node reboot. Investigation is slow because we have to stitch dmesg + journalctl + nv-smi dumps manually. Can we standardize a collector so triage is faster?
anya: Yes please. current process is: ssh -> sudo dmesg -T | grep -i xid -> journalctl -k -b -> run nvidia-smi queries. Takes too long during incidents.
mike: Agree. What would we want the collector to do specifically?
taylor: Minimal goals: 1) on Xid/ECC/driver-reset events capture: last 2k lines of dmesg, journalctl for nvidia/persistence/driver, full `nvidia-smi -q -x` and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,fan.temp,utilization.gpu,mem.used --format=csv` snapshots. 2) classify Xid codes into actionable categories (e.g., HW ECC, driver bug, timeout) and surface a suggested action: drain/replace/upgrade-driver. 3) upload to our artifact store (S3) with node id + short hash and return a JSON summary.
anya: +1. We also need RBAC/PII controls for uploads. Some customers run regulated workloads.
jacob: We should avoid big agents. A systemd unit + small script triggered by kernel oops or uevent sounds fine. Example hook: /etc/systemd/system/gpu-error-collector.service and a udev rule that runs it on `error` message from nvidia or when nvidia-persistenced reports a reset.
anya: Example commands to capture: 
```
# kernel messages
sudo dmesg -T --level=err,crit,warn | tail -n 2000
# journald for driver
sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -b --no-pager --lines=500
sudo journalctl -k -b | grep -i -E "NVRM|NVIDIA|Xid|GPU fault"
# nvml snapshot
sudo nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nvidia-smi-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).xml
```
mike: For parsing Xid codes we can map known ones (Xid 31 = GPU reset, Xid 13 often mem/ ECC?) — I'll add a small mapping table and heuristics: cluster-wide Xid bursts -> driver/firmware vs single-slot recurring Xid -> physical card.
taylor: Also want to capture PCIe AER logs and ECC counters: `sudo cat /sys/class/pci_bus/*/aer_*` and `grep 'Corrected' /sys/devices/*/edac* -R` if present.
jacob: Good call. For flaky cards, we should mark nodes with >3 resets in 24h as candidate-drain and create an automated ticket with the artifact link.
anya: How do we avoid false positives from software stress tests? Some jobs intentionally push memory and cause ECC correctable errors. We should correlate with job IDs using our scheduler tags (k8s pod annotations). Collector should try to attach recent container IDs via `crictl ps --labels` or `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase==Running -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.metadata.annotations}\n{end}'` where possible.
mike: That gets tricky in private deployments but doable for dedicated clusters. Fallback to host-only metadata when not available.
infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-node-22 reported 5 Xid 31 events in 1 hour. See artifacts: s3://redwood-gpu-errors/us-west-2/gpu-node-22/1747804521-5b2f.json
taylor: Nice — infra-bot already started uploading. Can we standardize the artifact JSON schema? We need flat fields: node, first_seen, last_seen, xid_codes[], actions_suggested[], artifact_url.
jacob: I'll draft a small schema and a parsing script (python) that ingests dmesg + nvxml and spits out that JSON. Use NVML parser (lxml) to extract driver version, GPU UUIDs, ECC counts.
mike: Parsing challenges: different driver versions change messages, and cloud-provider AMIs sometimes have modified kernel messages. We should include a fuzzy matching layer and a confidence score. Also store raw blobs for full context.
taylor: Ops ask: retention policy? right now we keep logs 30d in S3. For incidents we might want 90d. Any cost concerns?
anja: (typo) anya: Cost is small vs MTTR savings. But add a size cap per artifact (compress, gzip) and TTL tagging. We'll route large RAWs to cold storage.
mike: Implementation plan: 1) PR for collector script + systemd unit in infra/tools 2) add udev/systemd trigger, 3) infra-bot ingest hook to register artifact and run parser, 4) small dashboard showing recent Xid trends per region.
jacob: I'll open the PR and include tests for parsing Xid logs and a sample broken XML. Want reviewers: @mike and @taylor.
taylor: Thanks — once PR is in we can roll-out to canary pool and test with injected faults (stress-ng + nvml tests). :thumbsup:
anya: Also document runbook steps, what to look for in the JSON summary (driver version drift, ECC rising, repeated UUIDs).
infra-bot: NOTE: Scheduled job created: gpu-error-summarizer runs daily at 02:00 UTC and emits metrics to prometheus: redwood_gpu_xid_count_total{code="31",region="us-west-2"} etc.
mike: Great. I'll add Grafana panels and alert rules: more than 10 Xid31 per node in 6h -> page.
taylor: Perfect. Can we capture the initial message as a sample artifact? link: s3://redwood-gpu-errors/us-west-2/gpu-node-22/1747804521-raw.tgz
anya: I'll add RBAC for the bucket and a signed URL mechanism for on-call access.
taylor: Awesome work team, this should reduce triage time a lot. I'll kick off the canary roll tomorrow.
